title: Competitive Elections, Status Anxieties, and the Relative Strength of Ethnic versus National Identification in Africa

selected_claim.evidence_location: Table 3, Model 2 (logit), and Fig. 1; section “Does Political Competition Reduce National Identification in Africa?”
selected_claim.evidence_summary: The adjusted model estimates national identity as the outcome and includes election proximity, competitiveness categories, and their interaction. The negative interaction for elections with a victory margin below 10% (−0.019, p < 0.01) indicates that national identification declines as those competitive elections approach, relative to the >31% margin reference category. The paper reports this pattern as reduced national identification relative to ethnic identification.
selected_claim.x: Proximity to the closest presidential election (defined as −1 times the absolute number of months from the survey to the election), interacted with election competitiveness: victory margin <10%, 10–31%, or >31% (reference category).
selected_claim.y: Binary national-identity choice: 1 if the respondent said they felt more or only attached to their national identity than their ethnic identity, and 0 otherwise.
selected_claim.target_population: Afrobarometer respondents surveyed in rounds 2–7 (2004–2018) in the 17 included Sub-Saharan African countries: Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
selected_claim.adjustment_description: Table 3, Model 2 adjusts for the paper’s individual covariates and social-desirability-bias controls, and includes round fixed effects and time-trend controls. The model is a mixed-effects logit with country-level clustering/random intercepts and frequency weights.
covariates: Whether the respondent belongs to the country’s majority or plurality group

evidence_summary: The focal paper examines whether proximity to a competitive presidential election is associated with respondents’ relative national versus ethnic identity. The exposure is the survey’s temporal proximity to the closest presidential election (negative absolute months), interacted with election competitiveness categories defined by victory margin; the outcome is a binary choice indicating national identity is at least as salient as ethnic identity. The supplied claim specifies Table 3 Model 2 adjustment: individual covariates and social-desirability controls, round fixed effects and time trends, mixed-effects logit, country-level clustering/random intercepts, and frequency weights. The snapshot contains the focal exposure and outcome variables and the evidence queue was built from their selected conceptual groups.
x_definition: Electoral competition or closeness: degree to which an election is contested, including electoral victory margins and the intensity of competition across election contexts. The focal exposure additionally operationalizes timing as proximity to the closest presidential election and interacts this with competitiveness.
y_definition: Relative strength, salience, prioritization, or choice between national and ethnic identities, including whether national identity is at least as salient as ethnic identity.

splits.description: Relative salience, strength, prioritization, or choice between national and ethnic identity.

limitations: The supplied focal-claim description does not state the paper's empirical results, so no effect direction or magnitude is asserted here.
The claim describes the population and adjustment specification, but supplies no authors' caveats; these are not invented.

The exposure group captures electoral competitiveness/closeness but does not separately define temporal proximity to an election as a construct; this aspect is included in the focal measure and may not be represented by a distinct concept group.
2808 variables that earlier evaluations found miscoded in their concept groups were removed from those groups before analysis.
